title: New operations centre to include Planning and Development
subtitle: Also: trades event fee request, bridge weight limits, road resin trial, source protection nomination, water supply update.
overview: The committee's main item was an update on the new Township Operations Centre. It recommended a design that adds the Planning and Development Department, and asked staff to report back on other options, including future use of the farmhouse on the site {{vote:m9}}. The Mayor declared a conflict and left the room for this item.

Other recommendations affect roads and local services. The committee recommended a by-law allowing tractors with trailers to use a rural bridge under a multiple-unit load posting {{vote:m7}}, and a pilot with BioDiffusion Technologies to harden the base of Eighth Line West before repaving {{vote:m8}}. It recommended removing a holding zone on the Walser Building in Elora {{vote:m5}} and no objection to a longer licensed area at the Grand River Raceway for an August event {{vote:m10}}.

A request to waive rental fees for the Trade Tracks event went to staff for a report {{vote:m2}}. The Lake Erie source protection nomination was deferred for a staff report {{vote:m4}}. Members also heard a Water Supply Master Plan overview, and received the Treasurer's 2022 investment and interest-free loan statements and the Heritage Centre minutes for information.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended conceptual design Option 2, which adds the Planning and Development Department, and asked staff to report back on the alternatives discussed, including future use of the farmhouse.
The committee recommended adopting a by-law restricting vehicle weights on certain bridges, including a multiple-unit load posting so tractors pulling trailers can cross.

The committee recommended endorsing a trial with BioDiffusion Technologies on the Eighth Line West repaving and delegating authority for a Memorandum of Understanding to the Managing Director of Infrastructure Services.
The committee recommended removing the holding zone symbol at 6523 Wellington Road 7, Elora, and giving the by-law three readings.
The committee referred the South Wellington Community Lions request to waive rental fees for the Trade Tracks event to staff for a report.
The committee deferred selecting the municipal representative to the Lake Erie Region Source Protection Committee until staff can report, at the March Council or April committee meeting.
The committee recommended Council have no objection to the extended licensed area at the Grand River Raceway for the August 7, 2023 Industry Day event.

debate: On the Trade Tracks fee waiver, one councillor said fees have not been waived for other events and questioned whether Council could do so, suggesting a link to the upcoming community grants. Staff proposed a report, possibly in April, and the delegate said the event's costs were covered until then.

On the source protection nomination, members said they expected a chance to discuss appointments and for councillors to put names forward, and asked about reporting back and the per diem. Staff said the deadline was April 28 and a fuller report was available, so the committee deferred.

On the Operations Centre, one councillor was cautious about added cost for office space and asked why Planning and Development was not in the original space needs study, and about hybrid work. Staff cited recent planning legislation, a Civic Centre that is over capacity, and a hybrid program that had not eased space pressure.

Other councillors suggested a multi-storey building, community gardens, and a review of the future use of the farmhouse, and asked for money for Bellwood Hall. Staff said the financing relies mainly on development charges and land sales, with no impact on taxes or water rates.

On the BioDiffusion trial, councillors asked about cost, a guarantee and how long the road would be monitored. Staff said the supplier was reluctant to give a guarantee, so it is a short pilot, and long-term performance would need to be observed.
